name: Statistics
description: Describing data, sampling and estimation, hypothesis tests, regression and Bayesian and causal reasoning.

nodes.name: Data & sampling
nodes.desc: Types of variables, populations versus samples, sampling designs and sources of bias.
nodes.summary: You will be able to classify variables, distinguish populations from samples and recognise sampling designs and sources of bias.

nodes.name: Descriptive statistics
nodes.desc: Mean, median, mode, variance, standard deviation, quantiles and skew.
nodes.summary: You will be able to summarise data with measures of centre, spread, position and shape.

nodes.name: Plotting distributions
nodes.desc: Histograms, box plots, density plots and QQ plots for seeing the shape of data.
nodes.summary: You will be able to visualise the shape of data with histograms, box plots, density plots and QQ plots and read what they show.

nodes.name: Correlation
nodes.desc: Covariance, Pearson and Spearman correlation, and why correlation is not causation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to measure association with covariance and Pearson and Spearman correlation and avoid confusing correlation with causation.

nodes.name: Sampling distributions
nodes.desc: How a statistic varies from sample to sample and the idea of a standard error.
nodes.summary: You will understand how a statistic varies across repeated samples and be able to compute and interpret its standard error.

nodes.name: Central limit theorem
nodes.desc: Why sample means are approximately normal and when the approximation breaks down.
nodes.summary: You will be able to apply the central limit theorem to sample means and recognise when the normal approximation is unreliable.
topics: Statement of the central limit theorem

nodes.name: Point estimation
nodes.desc: Estimators, bias and variance, method of moments and maximum likelihood.
nodes.summary: You will be able to construct estimators by the method of moments and maximum likelihood and compare them by bias and variance.
topics: Bias, variance and mean squared error

nodes.name: Confidence intervals
nodes.desc: Constructing and correctly interpreting intervals for means and proportions.
nodes.summary: You will be able to construct confidence intervals for means and proportions and interpret their coverage correctly.
topics: Margin of error and sample size

nodes.name: Bootstrap
nodes.desc: Resampling to estimate standard errors and intervals without closed-form formulas.
nodes.summary: You will be able to estimate standard errors and confidence intervals by resampling when no closed-form formula is available.

nodes.name: Hypothesis testing
nodes.desc: Null and alternative hypotheses, test statistics, p-values, type I and II errors and power.
nodes.summary: You will be able to set up and carry out hypothesis tests and interpret p-values, error types and power correctly.
topics: Type I and type II errors

nodes.name: t-tests
nodes.desc: One-sample, two-sample and paired t-tests and their assumptions.
nodes.summary: You will be able to choose and run one-sample, two-sample and paired t-tests and check their assumptions.

nodes.name: Chi-square tests
nodes.desc: Goodness of fit and independence tests for categorical data.
nodes.summary: You will be able to test goodness of fit and independence for categorical data with chi-square tests.

nodes.name: ANOVA
nodes.desc: Comparing several group means with one-way and two-way analysis of variance.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compare several group means with one-way and two-way ANOVA and follow up with post-hoc tests.

nodes.name: Multiple testing
nodes.desc: Why many tests inflate false positives, with Bonferroni and false discovery rate control.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain why many tests inflate false positives and control errors with Bonferroni and false discovery rate methods.

nodes.name: Non-parametric tests
nodes.desc: Rank-based tests such as Mann-Whitney and Wilcoxon, and permutation tests.
nodes.summary: You will be able to use rank-based and permutation tests when parametric assumptions do not hold.

nodes.name: Linear regression
nodes.desc: Ordinary least squares, inference on coefficients, R-squared and interpreting effects.
nodes.summary: You will be able to fit linear regression by ordinary least squares, test coefficients and interpret effects and R-squared.
topics: Coefficient standard errors and t tests

nodes.name: Regression diagnostics
nodes.desc: Residual plots, heteroscedasticity, leverage, multicollinearity and transformations.
nodes.summary: You will be able to check regression assumptions with residual plots and fix problems such as heteroscedasticity and multicollinearity.

nodes.name: GLMs
nodes.desc: Generalised linear models: logistic and Poisson regression and link functions.
nodes.summary: You will be able to model binary and count outcomes with logistic and Poisson regression and interpret link functions.

nodes.name: A/B test analysis
nodes.desc: Analyse a simulated A/B test end to end, from power analysis to a decision memo.
nodes.summary: You will analyse a simulated A/B test end to end, from power analysis and sample sizing to a written decision memo.
topics: Running the test and computing intervals

nodes.name: Bayesian inference
nodes.desc: Priors, likelihoods and posteriors, conjugate models and credible intervals.
nodes.summary: You will be able to update priors into posteriors with Bayes' theorem, use conjugate models and report credible intervals.

nodes.name: Time series
nodes.desc: Trend, seasonality, autocorrelation and ARIMA-style forecasting.
nodes.summary: You will be able to decompose time series into trend and seasonality, examine autocorrelation and fit ARIMA-style forecasts.

nodes.name: Causal inference
nodes.desc: Confounding, randomised experiments, causal graphs and observational study designs.
nodes.summary: You will be able to reason about causal effects using randomised experiments, causal graphs and observational study designs.

nodes.name: Statistical study
nodes.desc: Plan, run and report a complete statistical analysis on a real dataset.
nodes.summary: You will plan, run and report a complete statistical analysis on a real dataset with clear conclusions.
